page: Microsoft Azure F64amds_v7 is an enterprise-grade virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates a single thread per core and supplies 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage is provided through a 7,559 GB integrated NVMe SSD volume, capable of handling low-latency I/O operations without reliance on external block devices. The instance operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and includes broad hardware instruction support such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results place this instance consistently in top-tier performance percentiles across compute, memory throughput, and storage-adjacent workloads. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 233,420.69 and an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 412.42 GB/sec, complemented by 193.26 GB/sec in uncached writes. Database handling capabilities are reinforced by 170.17 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and a static web serving throughput of 96.65 GB/sec. Large language model token throughput on the AMD CPU cores reached 5,641.46 prompt processing tokens per second on small 135M parameter models and 64.15 text generation tokens per second on medium 7B models.

The absence of dedicated GPU hardware makes this instance less suited for large-scale deep learning model training, yet its high physical core count, dense RAM ratio, and fast NVMe storage render it exceptionally cost-efficient for core-bound and memory-bound infrastructure. Optimal deployment targets include in-memory data grids, large relational and NoSQL databases, high-throughput web serving, real-time analytics, and heavy multi-threaded data compression pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure F64amds_v7 is a high-performance instance powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. It features 512.0 GB of system RAM, providing an expansive 8.0 GB per core, and includes an integrated 7,559 GB local NVMe SSD for high-bandwidth local caching and transient storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration flags. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-decile performance across multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 400 GB/sec, and 170.17 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking dedicated GPUs for accelerated model training, its substantial memory capacity, single-thread core dedication, and expansive NVMe volume make it a cost-effective, high-throughput solution for in-memory databases, batch processing, large-scale compilation, and distributed web services.
